% Figure 5 (S6): records improve the allocation only slowly across rounds.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}
\begin{axis}[
  width=0.82\textwidth, height=6.0cm,

  xmin=1, xmax=20, ymin=0, ymax=1,
  xtick={1, 5, 10, 15, 20},
  ytick={0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1},
  yticklabels={0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1},

  ylabel={correlation with optimal grants},
  ylabel style={font=\small}, xlabel style={font=\small},
  tick label style={font=\small},

\node[font=\small, anchor=west] at (axis cs:20.4,0.90) {with review};

\caption{Records do not catch up. The correlation of each funder's grants with the optimal grants, round by round, at the default parameters ($\tau_K = 1$, fifty simulated populations, twenty rounds). The records-only funder improves slowly, from 0.08 in the first round to 0.41 by round twenty, and remains further from the optimal allocation than the funder with the review signal is in round one (0.81). Under heavy-tailed capability the pattern is the same: 0.07 to 0.43, against 0.92.}
